assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos with IceCube opened a new observational window onto the universe, using a cubic-kilometre detector built in Antarctic ice. As an instrument-builder I find the originality of the detector concept and the clarity of the result compelling.
assessment.attribution: Only Francis Halzen is credited in the supplied entry. He is widely recognised as the driving intellectual and project leader, but a prize built on a large collaboration would normally want more than one name, and the supplied list gives no other credited individuals. A single-laureate configuration is possible but leaves the collaboration's many instrument builders unrecognised.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed through multiple analyses, the 2017 coincidence of a neutrino with the blazar TXS 0506+056, and later evidence for neutrinos from the Galactic plane and from active galaxies. The interpretation of the diffuse flux sources is still open, but the detection itself is firmly established and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether a single credited name can fairly represent a very large collaboration.
Source identification is only partially settled, and my recollection of recent IceCube results is from memory, not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The ATLAS and CMS discovery of the Higgs boson was the culmination of decades of detector development and confirmed the mechanism recognised by the 2013 prize. The detector design, calibration and trigger work were extraordinary, and the result is as solid as particle physics gets.
assessment.attribution: The three credited names are the recognised founding spokespersons and conceivers of ATLAS and CMS, which gives a balanced experimental configuration. Credit within collaborations of thousands is inherently hard to allocate, and other leaders (spokespersons and project leaders at the time of discovery) could be argued for, but the supplied three are a defensible set.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: two independent experiments, couplings measured over a decade, and the 2013 theory prize already stands. Recognition of the experimental side is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: The Nobel statutes and the collaboration-size issue make the choice of individuals contested.
Whether the committee wishes to recognise an experimental discovery of a particle whose theory was already honoured.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of gamma-ray burst afterglows with BeppoSAX, followed by optical and radio counterparts and redshifts, settled the extragalactic nature of GRBs and opened the era of multi-wavelength transient astronomy. It connects directly to X-ray and gamma-ray instrument work and is a very clear observational breakthrough.
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX detection of the X-ray afterglow and the rapid localisation, and Kulkarni led the optical, radio and redshift follow-up that established the cosmological distance. The three credited names map onto distinct decisive steps. Other contributors, for instance optical groups that first found the optical afterglow, may deserve consideration, and the supplied list may omit them.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by thousands of subsequent afterglow observations with Swift and Fermi and by the link to supernovae and to gravitational-wave counterparts. The physics is stable and well past the timeliness threshold, so this is mature, if arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit among the BeppoSAX team, optical discoverers and radio observers is shared, and I am recalling the history from memory.
Whether the prize should be framed as the instrument discovery or the astrophysical interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on the magic-wavelength idea, reached a fractional uncertainty at the 10^-18 level, which transformed precision metrology and enables tests of fundamental physics and relativistic geodesy. Pure measurement technique and systematics control of the kind I respect.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and Ye drove the performance to the best accuracy and stability. This is a clean two-person attribution. Other trapped-ion and optical clock pioneers have already been recognised by earlier prizes, and I rely on colleagues for atomic-physics credit details.
assessment.maturity: Many independent laboratories have built lattice clocks and agree at the highest precision, and a redefinition of the second is being discussed. Recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Relative weight against ion-clock work already honoured in 2012 and 2005.
My expertise in atomic physics is limited, so I defer to colleagues on credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire materials field, with very large impact and a new tunable platform.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction and Jarillo-Herrero the experimental discovery, which is a natural theory-plus-experiment pairing. Contributions by other experimental groups and by earlier theorists on twisted layers could also be argued.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups, with a rapidly growing literature. The microscopic origin of the superconductivity is not settled, so the field is still maturing, though the discovery itself is solid.
uncertainties: Condensed-matter credit boundaries are outside my expertise and I rely on colleagues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pulsar timing evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background gives a first look at a new band, probably from supermassive black-hole binaries. It rests on decades of precision timing, a measurement achievement I admire.
assessment.attribution: The credited names represent leadership of the NANOGrav, EPTA and PPTA collaborations, but credit is spread over several regional collaborations and many researchers, and the three-person selection is arguably arbitrary. Manchester's Parkes timing legacy is a reasonable anchor.
assessment.maturity: Evidence from several independent arrays in 2023, but at modest significance and without detection of individual sources or a firm source identification. Probably premature until confirmation by combined datasets.
uncertainties: Significance is evidence-level, not a firm discovery.
Origin could be cosmological rather than black-hole binaries.
Credit allocation across collaborations is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP produced precision full-sky CMB maps that fixed the cosmological parameters and established the standard Lambda-CDM model with percent-level accuracy. It was a landmark experiment, though a precision-measurement milestone rather than a new phenomenon.
assessment.attribution: Bennett led the mission, Page was a central instrument builder and Spergel led the cosmological analysis, so credit maps onto distinct roles. The earlier CMB prizes (2006, 2019) and the overlap with Planck complicate the claim.
assessment.maturity: Fully confirmed and superseded by Planck. Recognition would be late, and the committee may feel the subject was already covered.
uncertainties: Overlap with previously honoured CMB work.
Whether a precision refinement meets the originality bar.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED provides the basis of superconducting quantum processors and quantum sensing, with strong coupling of a qubit to a single microwave photon. It is influential and widely used, though I rely heavily on colleagues in this area.
assessment.attribution: Blais supplied the theory, Wallraff and Schoelkopf the first experimental demonstration, which is a fair theory-plus-experiment configuration. The 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits overlaps in subject and complicates timing and credit.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced across many laboratories and platforms. Highly mature as a technique, but the committee has just recognised nearby superconducting-circuit work.
uncertainties: I am deferring to colleagues in quantum information topics.
